newsitem.title: USA: New Britain, Conn, $112.2 mln debt sale delayed.
newsitem.headline: New Britain, Conn, $112.2 mln debt sale delayed.

text.p: New Britain's $112.2 million issue of taxable bonds, which was priced on Thursday only to be pulled a short time later, might not be reoffered for more than one month, the city's director of finance said.

The mayor, Lucian Pawlak, a Democrat, cancelled a meeting by the council, which was required under city law to approve the competitive bid, because some members did not get their notices on time. A quorum of 10 must approve such offers.

Susan McMullen said that had the meeting gone ahead, New Britain might have been at risk of a possible legal challenge, as the 15 council members must be served with the notices of the meeting 24 hours in advance.
John Jedrzejezyk, the director of finance, said that due to the objections of a few council members, the city will have to address their concerns and probably brief the entire council as well.

"We're going to spend some serious time with a couple of members, or with the entire council, going over the plan," he said, adding it was his speculation that this process might take "a month or two."

New Britain planned to issue the debt, which had a 2026 maturity that was priced at 85 basis points above the U.S. benchmark Treasuries, to fully fund about $109 million in unfunded pension liabilities.

Moody's Investors Service assigned the issue of general obligation bonds a rating of single-A, noting the new issue was "essentially replacement debt." The bonds will be substituted for pensions payments determined by actuaries over a 30-year period.

In its written report, however, the rating agency, added that the issue would impose certain risks on New Britain, as the city planned to enter a fixed-to-floating interest rate swap on a notional amount of $45.4 million.

Another risk Moody's identified was that by investing the bond proceeds at one time, the city would lose the benefit of dollar-cost-averaging, a strategy that aims to lessen the effects of the market's volatility.
